resources.string: Maps and map data are provided by Mapbox and OpenStreetMap contributors. Attribution is shown on the map itself as their licence requires.

This is an early build, but the core is real: territory claiming is live and server-authoritative. Ranking, missions, and squads are deliberately held back until the claim loop is proven on real walks.
Look up. Territory is not worth walking into traffic, and no hex is worth entering private property, construction sites, or rail corridors.
Claiming is disabled above walking speed. This is intentional — the game is not playable from a moving vehicle, and attempting it is dangerous.
If an area feels unsafe, leave it. The map will still be there tomorrow, and territory decays slowly enough that nothing is lost by waiting.
While the map is open we read your position, its accuracy, your speed, and whether Android reports the location as mocked.

These readings are sent to our servers to decide which hex you are standing in. The server makes that decision, not your phone, which is what stops a modified app from claiming territory it never walked to.

Every claim attempt is recorded with the reason it was accepted or rejected. That record is what lets us detect spoofed locations and impossible travel. It exists to protect honest players from people who fake their way to the top.
We do not track you in the background. We do not show your live position to other players. We do not sell location data, and there is no advertising SDK in this app.
Android will not ask again once permission has been denied. It has to be granted from system settings, or the map cannot tell which hex you are in.
How often the app asks for a position while the map is open. Faster updates make claiming feel more responsive and cost more battery.

Location is only read while the map is open. There is no background tracking, and no advertising identifier. Other players can see which ground you hold — never your live position, and never the route you walked to reach it.

If the app crashes, send a crash report so the fault can be fixed. That is a stack trace from the moment it crashed — never your location, nothing in the background, and no advertising identifier. Off by default.
Send a crash report when the app crashes.
These are real systems with real unlock conditions, not placeholders. Each one states what has to be true before it works.
Ground you walk becomes ground you hold.
The playable world is %1$s. Only ground inside the country can be claimed; the map is dimmed everywhere else.
The map needs your location to know which hex you are standing in. Territory is decided on our servers from the route you actually walk, which is what keeps it fair.
We do not track you in the background. Other players can see which ground you hold — never where you are now, and never where you have been.
Android will ask for permission next.

Preview mode runs the claim loop locally on this device so you can see what holding ground looks like. It is simulated: nothing is sent to the server, nothing is saved, and none of it becomes real territory.
Preview mode. Simulated territory, not real. Press exit to leave.

Your callsign and colour are computed from your account id, so they are the same on every device and after every reinstall. They are not stored as a profile and cannot be changed — which also means nobody can impersonate your colour on the map.
Without a session the server cannot attribute territory to you, so claiming is disabled. The map stays readable in the meantime.
You are not signed in, so the server cannot attribute territory to you. Sign-in uses a code sent to your email — this project has anonymous sign-in switched off.
Preview mode gives you a placeholder callsign so the map has something to colour. It is not a session, it is not stored anywhere, and it cannot hold real territory.
Sign-in is available now. Sign in with an email code and your callsign and colour become a real one, derived from your account — stable across devices and reinstalls, and able to hold territory.
WHY CAN I NOT CLAIM ANY GROUND?

Claiming is live. To claim a hex you must be signed in and standing inside Uzbekistan, on a real position fix at walking pace. If the button will not fire, open DIAGNOSTICS — it names the exact reason, whether that is no session, weak GPS, or being outside the country.
THE BUTTON SAYS GPS TOO WEAK
Your position is known to worse than 30 metres, which is wider than a hex. Acting on it could claim ground you are not standing on. Move away from tall buildings and give it a few seconds outdoors.
IT SAYS I AM MOVING TOO FAST
Claiming is limited to walking pace. This is deliberate: the game is not playable from a vehicle, and allowing it would be both unfair and unsafe.

Android is reporting your position as simulated. Turn off any location-spoofing app or developer mock-location setting. Spoofed positions are rejected by the server as well, so there is nothing to gain by hiding it.
THE MAP LOADS BUT NOTHING IS ON IT
That is expected. No territory exists anywhere yet, for any player.
Location is only read while the map is open. If the cost is still too high, lower the tracking cadence in settings — claiming stays available, it just updates less often.
Territory has to belong to someone. We send a six-digit code to sign you in — there is no password to remember and nothing to install.
Signing in. That is all. Your address is not shown to other players, not used for marketing, and not linked to your location history.
We emailed a 6-digit code to %1$s. It expires shortly.
A new code has been sent.
Check spam. Delivery depends on the mail service this project is configured with, so it can take a moment.

A territory board — every hex held, with its borders and decay at a glance — is deliberately held back until enough ground is in play to be worth its own screen. Territory lives on the map itself for now.
Enough ground is held to make a dedicated board worth opening.
Watch the map. That is where territory sits today.
A ranking is only meaningful once territory can be won and lost. Ranking players on zero captured hexes would rank nobody against nobody.
Enough ground has been claimed to rank.
Nothing to compare yet — no ground has been claimed.
Alerts matter once your ground comes under attack often enough to warrant them. The system is held back until there is enough territory in play — and there is nothing to report yet.
Territory changes hands often enough for an alert to earn its interruption.

Missions assign and score objectives on top of the claim loop. They are held back until that loop is proven fun on real walks — an objective bolted onto a loop nobody enjoys would only disguise the problem.
The claim loop is proven, so an objective adds to it.
Walk and hold ground. That is the whole objective today.
Teams and empires are deliberately held back. Alliances built before the solo loop is proven fun would hide whether the loop is fun at all.
The walk-claim-hold loop is proven on real walks by real players.
Hold ground alone first. That is the part that has to work.
There is nothing to sell, and nothing worth buying. A shop opened before the game is good is just a way to take money for an unproven product.
The loop is proven and cosmetics exist worth owning.
Nothing here will ever affect who wins ground. Cosmetics only.

Cosmetics only, forever. Nothing sold here will ever affect who holds ground, how fast you claim it, or how far you can walk. Ground is won on foot or it is not won. That rule is the reason this surface is still shut: a store is easy, and a store worth trusting is not.

Not checked yet. This resolves once a position fix is accepted.
Preview mode is active. Everything you claim is simulated on this device, held in memory, and discarded when you leave. Nothing is sent to the server and none of it is real territory.

The capture backend is live and server-authoritative. Claiming a hex submits your raw position; the server derives the cell, enforces the anti-cheat gates, and records the attempt. Everything you claim is real.
Email is the only sign-in route on this project, and no code has been confirmed as arriving on this device. So sign-in is UNPROVEN rather than available — an enabled provider is not a working one.
Sign-in configuration has not been checked yet. Press RE-CHECK.
Asking the server which sign-in methods it accepts.
The server did not answer when asked how sign-in is configured, so these rows read UNKNOWN rather than guessing. %1$s
Accounts are not auto-confirmed on this project, so a code must genuinely arrive by email before anyone can sign in. Mail delivery is therefore required, not optional.
No sign-in code has ever been requested from this install, so whether email works here is still untested. Requesting one from the SIGN IN screen is the test.

The server accepted a request to send a code, but no code has been successfully entered yet. That means delivery is UNPROVEN — an accepted request is not an arrived email. If nothing reached the inbox, the mail service configured for this project is where to look.
A code reached this address and was accepted. Email delivery is proven to work on this project.
The last send attempt was refused. %1$s
A delivery record exists on this device but could not be read — most likely written by a different version of the app. Treat delivery as unproven and request a fresh code.
a code is already being sent

Held ground reads UNKNOWN until ownership is read back from the server, and rank needs the leaderboard, which is not open yet. Neither is shown as zero, because zero would be a claim about you rather than about the data.
No badges exist yet. They are awarded by the server for ground held over time, so the first one becomes possible when capture and ownership are both live — not when this screen is redesigned.
Nothing has been recorded yet. Records are written from claims the server accepted, so this fills in from real walking rather than from anything stored on this device.
A profile picture is a Pro capability. Until then your crest is your face — it is derived from your identity, so it is already unarguably yours.
Pro cannot be bought yet: this build has no payment integration. Nothing here is a purchase prompt, and no entitlement can be granted until there is a server able to verify one.
Every badge is earned from real claims the server accepts — nothing here is awarded for opening the app. Capture is not live yet, so none are earned. This is the cabinet you are playing toward.

Your history begins at your first accepted claim. Until capture is live there is nothing to record, so every line reads unknown rather than zero — a zero would be a claim about you, not about the data.

Pro never buys an advantage in taking ground. Every benefit is cosmetic, an account convenience, or a fuller view of your own history. Ground is won on foot or it is not won — that rule is not for sale.
no billing integration in this build
